# Overview

This document covers the **data preparation stage** for VAST Challenge 2026 Mini-Challenge 2 (MC2). The task is to reconstruct the chain of events that led to the anomalous SaidIt post sent by **John Windward** on **May 17, 2046 at 4:21am**.

Before any analysis can happen, the raw data needs to be:

1.  Loaded efficiently and inspected,
2.  Flattened from its nested JSON structure into tidy tables,
3.  Cleaned (timestamps converted, duplicates checked, missingness understood),
4.  Joined with the organisation chart so that every actor in an event can be traced back to their **department**, **team**, and **human principal** (for autonomous agents).

The end product of this stage is a single enriched events table (`events_mapped`) plus several lookup tables. Along the way we render several descriptive visuals so the shape of the data is intuitive before any modelling begins.

# Setup

## Loading R packages

The packages below cover the jobs we do in this notebook: read JSON (`jsonlite`), wrangle in the tidyverse, handle timestamps (`lubridate`), walk the org chart as a graph (`tidygraph`, `ggraph`), and render the report tables and plots (`DT`, `gt`, `scales`, `patchwork`).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(jsonlite, tidyverse, lubridate,
               tidygraph, ggraph,
               DT, gt, scales, patchwork)
```
:::


## Reading the raw data

The JSON files are large and slow to re-parse on every render. The convention is to parse JSON **once** with `fromJSON()`, then cache as `.rds` (R's native binary format, smaller and faster, and it preserves column types). The `if (!file.exists(...))` guard means the conversion runs only the first time.

> Note on filenames: the MC2 data description refers to `MC2_Data.json`. Confirm the actual filename with `list.files("data")` before running the chunk; the code below uses lowercase `mc2_data.json`, change it to match what you have on disk.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (!file.exists("data/mc2_data.rds")) {
  mc2_data <- fromJSON("data/mc2_data.json")
  write_rds(mc2_data, "data/mc2_data.rds")
}
if (!file.exists("data/org_chart.rds")) {
  org_chart <- fromJSON("data/org_chart.json")
  write_rds(org_chart, "data/org_chart.rds")
}
```
:::

## Visualising the organisation chart

A picture of the org tree is the single most useful reference for this whole project, because every actor in the event log eventually needs to be located somewhere on it. We highlight **John Windward** in red so his place in the structure is immediately visible.

The layout is `dendrogram`, which gives a tidy top down tree. Node colour shows the `type`, and the label is shifted slightly below each node for readability.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
org_graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = org_nodes,
                       edges = org_edges,
                       directed = TRUE)

org_graph <- org_graph %>% 
  mutate(is_jw = (id == "person:john_windward"),
         display_label = label)

ggraph(org_graph, layout = "dendrogram", circular = FALSE) +
  geom_edge_diagonal(alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(colour = type, size = is_jw)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = display_label,
                     fontface = ifelse(is_jw, "bold", "plain")),
                 size = 2.6, vjust = 1.6, hjust = 0.5) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 2.5, `TRUE` = 5), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 30, 10),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Tenant Thread organisation chart",
       subtitle = "John Windward (Customer Support, Department Lead) shown larger and bold",
       colour = "Node type")
```

## Department size summary

Before moving on, a quick bar chart of how many people sit in each department, so we know which parts of the org are heavy and which are light.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# helper: all node ids reachable downward from start_id
descendants_of <- function(start_id, edges_df) {
  out <- character(0); frontier <- start_id
  while (length(frontier) > 0) {
    children <- edges_df %>% filter(source %in% frontier) %>% pull(target)
    out <- c(out, children); frontier <- children
  }
  unique(out)
}

person_ids_set <- org_nodes %>% filter(type == "person") %>% pull(id)

dept_sizes <- org_nodes %>% 
  filter(type == "department") %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(n_people = sum(descendants_of(id, org_edges) %in% person_ids_set)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(department = label, n_people) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_people))

ggplot(dept_sizes, aes(x = n_people, y = reorder(department, n_people))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_people), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "People per department",
       x = "Number of people", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Cleaning the events table

## Convert timestamps and add row id

Working with Unix timestamps is painful for filtering by date. We convert `when` into a `POSIXct` datetime in UTC, then derive a `date` and `hour` column for easier grouping. We also keep an explicit `event_id` (the original `id` field) and a sequential `row` index for ordering.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
events_clean <- mc2_events %>% 
  mutate(
    event_id  = id,
    datetime  = as_datetime(when, tz = "UTC"),
    date      = as_date(datetime),
    hour      = hour(datetime),
    .keep = "unused"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(row = row_number(), .before = 1)

events_clean %>% 
  select(row, event_id, datetime, short_name) %>% 
  head(5)
```

## Distribution of events over time

A histogram of when things happened across May 2046 tells us whether activity is steady or spiky. A red dashed line marks the moment of the anomalous SaidIt post (2046-05-17 04:21 UTC), so we can see immediately whether there is unusual activity around it.

# Building lookup tables from `org_chart`

## Person lookup with department and team

The org chart is a tree: `company > department > team > person`, except for department leads (like John Windward) who hang directly under a department rather than under a team. We walk down from each department to build a flat lookup that, for every person, gives us their team and department.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dept_ids <- org_nodes %>% filter(type == "department") %>% pull(id)

person_lookup <- map_dfr(dept_ids, function(d) {
  desc <- descendants_of(d, org_edges)
  tibble(department_id = d, descendant_id = desc)
}) %>% 
  inner_join(org_nodes %>% filter(type == "person"),
             by = c("descendant_id" = "id"))

# team for each person (if any)
team_ids <- org_nodes %>% filter(type == "team") %>% pull(id)

person_team <- map_dfr(team_ids, function(t) {
  desc <- descendants_of(t, org_edges)
  tibble(team_id = t, descendant_id = desc)
}) %>% 
  inner_join(org_nodes %>% filter(type == "person"),
             by = c("descendant_id" = "id")) %>% 
  select(person_id = descendant_id, team_id)

person_lookup <- person_lookup %>% 
  transmute(
    person_id     = descendant_id,
    person_name   = label,
    title         = title,
    department_id = department_id
  ) %>% 
  left_join(person_team, by = "person_id") %>% 
  left_join(org_nodes %>% filter(type == "department") %>% 
              select(department_id = id, department_name = label),
            by = "department_id") %>% 
  left_join(org_nodes %>% filter(type == "team") %>% 
              select(team_id = id, team_name = label),
            by = "team_id")
```

## Agent to principal lookup (derived from events)

Autonomous agents (`agent:*` IDs) are **not** in the org chart, they only show up inside `mc2_events`. To attach an agent to a human, we look at events where agents and persons co-appear in `parties`. For each (agent, person) pair, the most frequent human co-actor is taken as the agent's likely principal.

> This is a heuristic. If the data contains explicit assignment events (look at the `short_name` list above for things like `agent_created`, `agent_assigned`, etc.), those should be preferred as the source of truth.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
agent_principal_pairs <- events_long %>% 
  filter(actor_kind %in% c("agent", "person")) %>% 
  select(row, actor_kind, actor_id) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = actor_kind, values_from = actor_id,
              values_fn = list) %>% 
  unnest_longer(agent, values_to = "agent_id") %>% 
  unnest_longer(person, values_to = "person_id") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(agent_id), !is.na(person_id)) %>% 
  count(agent_id, person_id, name = "co_occurrences") %>% 
  arrange(desc(co_occurrences))

agent_principal_pairs %>% head(10)
```

# Master enriched table

Now we join everything. Each (event, actor) row gets enriched with department, team, and title for persons, and for agents with their inferred principal plus that principal's department and team.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
events_mapped <- events_long %>% 
  left_join(person_lookup,
            by = c("actor_id" = "person_id")) %>% 
  rename(actor_person_name = person_name,
         actor_title       = title,
         actor_department  = department_name,
         actor_team        = team_name) %>% 
  select(-department_id, -team_id)

events_mapped <- events_mapped %>% 
  left_join(agent_lookup %>% select(agent_id, principal_id),
            by = c("actor_id" = "agent_id")) %>% 
  left_join(person_lookup %>% 
              select(principal_id   = person_id,
                     principal_name = person_name,
                     principal_title = title,
                     principal_department = department_name,
                     principal_team = team_name),
            by = "principal_id")

events_mapped <- events_mapped %>% 
  mutate(
    effective_person_id   = coalesce(if_else(actor_kind == "person", actor_id, NA_character_),
                                     principal_id),
    effective_person_name = coalesce(actor_person_name, principal_name),
    effective_department  = coalesce(actor_department, principal_department),
    effective_team        = coalesce(actor_team, principal_team),
    effective_title       = coalesce(actor_title, principal_title)
  )

events_mapped %>% 
  select(row, event_id, datetime, short_name, actor_kind, actor_id,
         effective_person_name, effective_department, effective_team) %>% 
  head(10)
```
